claims.text: In-situ build-platform preheating to approximately 400°C during LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi powder will reduce residual thermal stresses.
In-situ build-platform preheating to approximately 400°C will improve the mechanical properties of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi components.
Preheating moderates the thermal gradient during LPBF.
A moderated thermal gradient promotes a more uniform microstructure.
A moderated thermal gradient reduces directional grain anisotropy.
An elevated build-platform temperature decreases the temperature difference between the melt pool and the substrate.
Decreasing the temperature difference between the melt pool and substrate lowers the cooling rate.
The reduction in cooling rate limits thermal-contraction stresses.
Reducing steep thermal gradients lowers residual stress.
Lower cooling rates and thermal gradients improve the overall mechanical integrity of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi components.
Preheated components will have significantly lower residual stress than components produced by LPBF without platform preheating.
Preheated components will have greater ductility than components produced by LPBF without platform preheating.
Preheated components will have greater strength than components produced by LPBF without platform preheating.
The proposed improvement is applicable around a platform temperature of 400°C for miniature LPBF components.
The results may change for other geometries or upon scale-up.
Nonuniform build-plate heating could produce localized microstructural variations and defects.
The magnitude of the performance improvement depends on precise control of the thermal environment.
